question.problem: Approximately $20%$ of the emails received in an account are spam. If there are $20$ inbox emails, what is the standard deviation of the number of spam emails received? Round your answer to $3$ decimal places.
question.worked_solution:
Let the random variable $X$ be equal to the number of spam emails.

Here, we have the following information:

- there are $n=20$ inbox emails

- the probability of being a spam email is $p=20%=0.20$

So, $X$ follows a binomial distribution, where $X∼B(20,0.20).$ 

For a binomial random variable $X,$ the standard deviation is given by

$$
\text{SD}[X]=\sqrt{\text{Var}[X]}=\sqrt{np(1-p)}
$$

where $n$ is the number of experiments and $p$ is the probability of success on each experiment.

So, the standard deviation of the number of spam emails received is

$$
\begin{aligned}\text{SD}[X] & =\sqrt{np(1-p)} \\  & =\sqrt{(20)(0.20)(1-0.20)} \\  & =\sqrt{3.2} \\  & =1.789\end{aligned}
$$

rounded to $3$ decimal places.
